answer: Proof-of-silicon identity minting: an identity is issued only with a fresh hardware-enclave attestation quote binding it to one physical chip. The network treats quotes like bedrock shale — layered, inspectable, unforgeable at scale. New identities enter through a single narrow inlet: a registry verifying quotes against manufacturer revocation lists, one mint per device per epoch. The attacker faces a ferrous reality: N identities demand N real chips, so marginal cost jumps from near-zero compute to hardware procurement. Copied quotes fail, since each quote is nonce-bound to its session.
